spec: CONTROL.md §6 prompt, One at a time, in the order they were sent
note: The order a machine delivers one session's messages in. Each case is a run of steps: `arrive` is one poll's answer, its messages listed as the receiver listed them and all taken in hand together (`iat` is the signed time, in milliseconds); `done` is the message whose turn it is finishing, however it ends (answered, failed, stopped by a cancel); `drop` is a message that turns out to have no delivery while it waits or as its turn comes (refused, expired). `expect` is the order the messages are given their turn in. A message is given its turn only when no message of its session has one; then the earliest-signed of those waiting goes, and of two signed in the same millisecond the one that arrived first. Nothing here depends on how long a message's verification, download or wait for its session's start takes.

cases.name: two of one poll, nothing running: in the order the poll lists them when that is the order they were signed in
behind a running turn: two that arrive in one poll wait, and go in sent order (2026-11-10: bravo, charlie, delta)
a poll that lists them out of the order they were signed in: by signing time, even with nothing running
a later poll brings one signed before those already waiting: it goes ahead of them
signed in the same millisecond: the one that arrived first
one that has its turn keeps it: an earlier-signed message that arrives later waits for it
one refused while it waits, and one refused as its turn comes, give their places up: the rest keep their order
each session has its own line: one session's running turn holds up nobody else's message
